gaps.sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

gaps.sentence: 'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).

gaps.sentence: 'I saw the accident happen,' the witness stated. The witness stated that he ___ the accident happen.
gaps.explanation: Past simple backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb: saw → had seen.

gaps.sentence: 'We won't stay long,' they said. They said they ___ stay long.
gaps.explanation: will not → would not (wouldn't) after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

gaps.sentence: 'You may leave early,' the manager said. The manager said we ___ leave early.
'Get out of my way!' the guard snapped. The guard snapped at me ___ out of my way.
gaps.hint: snap at sb to do sth
gaps.explanation: The order is reported as snapped at me + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Shall I close the window?' he asked. He asked ___ close the window.
gaps.explanation: Shall I...? (offering) becomes if/whether he should... in reported speech.
